summary: The note surveys a season of book and poetry festivals from autumn 2023, arguing that literary events still draw enthusiastic crowds despite digital distractions. It lists each festival with dates, featured authors and poets, and activities such as workshops, readings, auctions and theatrical talks. Events range from The Word Gala and Metropolitan Poetry Circus to the Grand Literary Bazaar, the Emerging Writers Weekend, and children's and political poetry events.
one_line: A guide to autumn 2023 book and poetry festivals, with dates, featured writers and activities, celebrating the enduring power of the written word.
key_facts: The Word Gala is scheduled for October 10th to 15th, 2023, and James Harrington, author of "Whispers of the Clandestine," is slated to open it.
The Word Gala also features Claire Sterling, with a sequel to "The Orchid Keeper," and debut author Miguel Santos, whose "Under a Tamarind Sky" has a cult following.
The Word Gala culminates in fireside readings under starlight, a cherished tradition.
The Metropolitan Poetry Circus begins November 1st and runs 14 days, featuring Aria Thompson, Griffin Morø and S. R. Khorana.
Metropolitan Poetry Circus workshops include "Sonnet Crafting" and "The Power of Performance."
The Emerging Writers Weekend is scheduled for December 3rd-5th and features Ryanne O'Connor, whose debut novel is "Sea Glass Hearts."
The Emerging Writers Weekend has 'In-Conversation' segments hosted by book critic Harlan Z. Smith and offers manuscript preparation clinics and publishing guidance.
The Grand Literary Bazaar runs November 27th to 29th, the weekend after Thanksgiving, under the arches of the historic Grand Hall.

The Bazaar's annual auction features manuscripts and letters; last year a letter by poet laureate Eliana Brooks fetched a staggering sum, and this year includes an annotated script by screenwriter Daniel Ward.
The Literary Landscape series on September 21st in outdoor amphitheaters focuses on theatrical adaptations, with novelist Elliot Greene among the speakers.
The "Literary Eclipses" segment features Sophie Lorraine, who took a seven-year publishing hiatus and returned with a Pulitzer nomination.
The Political Poet's Platform on December 12th is a daylong event featuring Lila D'Souza, author of "Shards of a Nation," and poet-activist Ramon Torres.
The Children's Literature Fiesta is set for December 15th-17th with interactive readings, character parades and games, featuring Maria Mendoza and Max & Lily Harper.
